papers.title: Estimation of spatio-temporal temperature evolution during laser spot melting using in-situ dynamic x-ray radiography
papers.abstract: Understanding the spatio-temporal evolution of thermal gradient (G) at and velocity (R) of the solid-liquid and liquid-vapor interfaces is critical for the control of site-specific microstructures in additive manufacturing. In-situ dynamic x-ray radiography (DXR) has been used in recent years to probe the evolution of R with high spatial and temporal resolutions. However, the current methods used to measure the temperature (and therefore, G) are inadequate for sub-melt-pool surface measurement (e.g. thermography) or have lower resolution or limited field-of-view (e.g. x-ray diffraction). In this study, we demonstrate a novel approach to estimate the sub-surface temperature distribution and its time evolution with significantly higher resolutions using DXR data. This methodology uses the Beer-Lambert's law as a physical basis and is demonstrated using an in-situ laser spot-melting experiment on Ti-6Al-4V alloy.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究激光熔融过程的温度演化估计方法，未涉及生物医学植入物的应力屏蔽、疲劳或表面形态等关键问题。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address porous structure design, stress shielding, mechanical testing, or osseointegration for biomedical implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过X射线成像估计激光熔融过程中温度场演变，以控制微观结构。
summary_zh.method: 利用Beer-Lambert定律从动态X射线辐射数据反演亚表面温度分布。
summary_zh.result: 实现了高分辨率温度场估计，验证了方法的可行性。
summary_zh.validation: 采用Ti-6Al-4V合金的激光定点熔融实验进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To estimate spatio-temporal temperature distribution during laser spot melting using in-situ dynamic x-ray radiography for microstructure control.
summary_en.method: A novel approach based on Beer-Lambert law to reconstruct sub-surface temperature fields from DXR data.
summary_en.result: Successfully demonstrated high-resolution temperature estimation during laser melting of Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.validation: Validated using an in-situ laser spot melting experiment on Ti-6Al-4V alloy.

papers.title: Seeing Through the Grass: Semantic Pointcloud Filter for Support Surface Learning
papers.abstract: Mobile ground robots require perceiving and understanding their surrounding support surface to move around autonomously and safely. The support surface is commonly estimated based on exteroceptive depth measurements, e.g., from LiDARs. However, the measured depth fails to align with the true support surface in the presence of high grass or other penetrable vegetation. In this work, we present the Semantic Pointcloud Filter (SPF), a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that learns to adjust LiDAR measurements to align with the underlying support surface. The SPF is trained in a semi-self-supervised manner and takes as an input a LiDAR pointcloud and RGB image. The network predicts a binary segmentation mask that identifies the specific points requiring adjustment, along with estimating their corresponding depth values. To train the segmentation task, 300 distinct images are manually labeled into rigid and non-rigid terrain. The depth estimation task is trained in a self-supervised manner by utilizing the future footholds of the robot to estimate the support surface based on a Gaussian process. Our method can correctly adjust the support surface prior to interacting with the terrain and is extensively tested on the quadruped robot ANYmal. We show the qualitative benefits of SPF in natural environments for elevation mapping and traversability estimation compared to using raw sensor measurements and existing smoothing methods. Quantitative analysis is performed in various natural environments, and an improvement by 48% RMSE is achieved within a meadow terrain.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究机器人地形感知，与有限元代理建模无关。
llm.why_not_core: No finite element analysis, surrogate modeling, or optimization; purely robotics perception.

summary_zh.motivation: 在植被环境中移动机器人需要准确感知支撑表面。
summary_zh.method: 提出语义点云滤波器SPF，利用CNN和半自监督学习调整激光雷达测量值。
summary_zh.result: 在草地地形中均方根误差降低48%。
summary_zh.validation: 在四足机器人ANYmal上进行了实地测试。

summary_en.motivation: Mobile robots require accurate support surface estimation in vegetated terrain.
summary_en.method: The Semantic Pointcloud Filter uses a CNN with semi-self-supervised learning to adjust LiDAR measurements.
summary_en.result: Achieves 48% RMSE improvement in meadow terrain.
summary_en.validation: Validated on the quadruped robot ANYmal in natural environments.

papers.title: Neural operator for structural simulation and bridge health monitoring
papers.abstract: Infusing deep learning with structural engineering has received widespread attention for both forward problems (structural simulation) and inverse problems (structural health monitoring). Based on Fourier Neural Operator, this study proposes VINO (Vehicle-bridge Interaction Neural Operator) to serve as the digital twin of bridge structures. VINO learns mappings between structural response fields and damage fields. In this study, VBI-FE dataset was established by running parametric finite element (FE) simulations considering a random distribution of structural initial damage field. Subsequently, VBI-EXP dataset was produced by conducting an experimental study under four damage scenarios. After VINO was pre-trained by VBI-FE and fine-tuned by VBI-EXP from the bridge at the healthy state, the model achieved the following two improvements. First, forward VINO can predict structural responses from damage field inputs more accurately than the FE model. Second, inverse VINO can determine, localize, and quantify damages in all scenarios, suggesting the practicality of data-driven approaches.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文提出的神经算子方法可迁移至生物力学FEA代理建模，但研究背景为桥梁结构而非植入物设计，缺少不确定性量化和多目标约束处理。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not apply to biomedical or implant design; lacks uncertainty quantification and multi-objective constrained optimization; validation is on bridge structures, not biomechanical FEA.

summary_zh.motivation: 提出神经算子作为桥梁结构数字孪生。
summary_zh.method: 基于傅里叶神经算子，训练正向和反向预测模型。
summary_zh.result: 正向预测响应优于有限元，反向能损伤定位定量。
summary_zh.validation: 有限元仿真数据集和桥梁实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a neural operator as a digital twin for bridge structures for both forward simulation and inverse damage identification.
summary_en.method: A Fourier Neural Operator (VINO) is trained on parametric FE simulations and fine-tuned with experimental data from a bridge.
summary_en.result: The forward model predicts structural responses more accurately than the FE model, and the inverse model successfully localizes and quantifies damage.
summary_en.validation: The model is validated using a dataset of parametric FE simulations and an experimental study on a bridge with four damage scenarios.

papers.title: Learning to Learn Unlearned Feature for Brain Tumor Segmentation
papers.abstract: We propose a fine-tuning algorithm for brain tumor segmentation that needs only a few data samples and helps networks not to forget the original tasks. Our approach is based on active learning and meta-learning. One of the difficulties in medical image segmentation is the lack of datasets with proper annotations, because it requires doctors to tag reliable annotation and there are many variants of a disease, such as glioma and brain metastasis, which are the different types of brain tumor and have different structural features in MR images. Therefore, it is impossible to produce the large-scale medical image datasets for all types of diseases. In this paper, we show a transfer learning method from high grade glioma to brain metastasis, and demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves balanced parameters for both glioma and brain metastasis domains within a few steps.

summary_en.method: A fine-tuning algorithm combining active learning and meta-learning is proposed.
summary_en.result: The method achieves balanced parameters for both glioma and brain metastasis domains with few samples.

papers.title: An Active Learning-based Approach for Hosting Capacity Analysis in Distribution Systems
papers.abstract: With the increasing amount of distributed energy resources (DERs) integration, there is a significant need to model and analyze hosting capacity (HC) for future electric distribution grids. Hosting capacity analysis (HCA) examines the amount of DERs that can be safely integrated into the grid and is a challenging task in full generality because there are many possible integration of DERs in foresight. That is, there are numerous extreme points between feasible and infeasible sets. Moreover, HC depends on multiple factors such as (a) adoption patterns of DERs that depend on socio-economic behaviors and (b) how DERs are controlled and managed. These two factors are intrinsic to the problem space because not all integration of DERs may be centrally planned, and could largely change our understanding about HC. This paper addresses the research gap by capturing the two factors (a) and (b) in HCA and by identifying a few most insightful HC scenarios at the cost of domain knowledge. We propose a data-driven HCA framework and introduce active learning in HCA to effectively explore scenarios. Active learning in HCA and characteristics of HC with respect to the two factors (a) and (b) are illustrated in a 3-bus example. Next, detailed large-scale studies are proposed to understand the significance of (a) and (b). Our findings suggest that HC and its interpretations significantly change subject to the two factors (a) and (b).

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究配电网的分布式能源接入容量分析，与生物力学有限元代理建模完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses power system hosting capacity analysis with active learning, lacking any biomechanics, implant design, FEA surrogate modeling, or experimental validation relevant to the user's direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 考虑社会行为和控制因素，提升配电网分布式能源接入容量分析的准确性。
summary_zh.method: 提出主动学习框架，有效探索高维场景以识别关键极限点。
summary_zh.result: 接入容量及其解释显著依赖于社会行为和控制因素。
summary_zh.validation: 在3节点算例中验证，并计划大规模研究。

summary_en.motivation: To improve hosting capacity analysis in distribution systems by incorporating socio-economic adoption patterns and control strategies of distributed energy resources.
summary_en.method: A data-driven active learning framework is proposed to efficiently explore the high-dimensional scenario space and identify critical feasibility boundaries.
summary_en.result: Hosting capacity and its interpretations change significantly when considering adoption patterns and control factors.
summary_en.validation: Illustrated on a 3-bus example system; large-scale studies are proposed but not performed.
